name: The Shins
label: Sub Pop
lede: A shy guy's side project from an Albuquerque basement that got sold to McDonald's, handed to Natalie Portman, pushed to No. 2 on the Billboard chart, and then rebuilt from scratch by the only member left.

eras.title: Albuquerque, a basement and a side project
eras.text: James Mercer spent the '90s in Flake Music, a four-way band in a city nobody's A&R reps visited. The Shins started as his side project, and by 2000 it was the only thing he cared about, even as Albuquerque wore him down.

years.h: James Mercer starts Flake Music in Albuquerque
years.p: James Mercer, Jesse Sandoval, Marty Crandall and Neal Langford form Flake Music. They release the Spork EP and an album on Omnibus Records and tour with [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]] and [[Califone|68025033-de1b-42f5-8a21-bedfb8895dda]].
years.xp: Flake Music's album was When You Land Here, It's Time to Return. It was reissued in November 2014.

years.h: The Shins begin as a James Mercer and Jesse Sandoval duo
years.p: While Flake Music carries on, James Mercer starts a side project with drummer Jesse Sandoval, opening as a two-piece for Cibo Matto and [[The American Analog Set|7f5dde96-1573-4491-9673-f03fe7c5caaa]]. Unlike Flake Music, Mercer writes everything.

years.h: Nature Bears a Vacuum, The Shins' first 7-inch
years.p: Omnibus Records releases The Shins' debut 7-inch. A second single, When I Goose-Step, follows, then a tour with [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]].

years.h: Flake Music ends and The Shins become a four-piece
years.p: Flake Music breaks up and bassist Neal Langford and keyboardist Marty Crandall move over to The Shins. Early members Dave Hernandez and Ron Skrasek go back to their band Scared of Chaka.

years.h: Isaac Brock and Zeke Howard mail out The Shins' demos
years.p: James Mercer is stuck and depressed in Albuquerque, obsessing over a debut album. Friends [[Isaac Brock|071d3d16-8ed7-4e06-be96-2c52defcf434]] of Modest Mouse and Zeke Howard of [[Love as Laughter|8f5c6093-27ba-402d-b092-4157c93a4104]] send his cassette demos to labels.

eras.title: One single, then a hamburger ad
eras.text: A one-off Sub Pop single turned into a record deal, and a record made in a basement turned into the indie album of the moment. Then McDonald's paid for New Slang, and the band's hometown alt-weekly didn't like it.

years.cap: The Shins at House of Blues, Dallas · Wikimedia
q: All of a sudden my whole life was up in smoke.
years.h: Jonathan Poneman offers The Shins one Sub Pop single: "New Slang"
years.p: Sub Pop co-founder Jonathan Poneman sees The Shins open for Modest Mouse in San Francisco and offers a one-off single. New Slang goes out to the Sub Pop Singles Club in February 2001, and Sub Pop signs the band.
years.xp: James Mercer's life turned over at once: he signed, quit his job, left town, and a five-year relationship ended.

years.h: Oh, Inverted World comes out on Sub Pop
years.p: The Shins' debut, mostly recorded in James Mercer's basement before Sub Pop ever called. Critics hear '60s pop through a skewed lens and Albuquerque suddenly has a band people talk about.
years.xp: Mercer says his favorite is the closer, The Past and Pending, because it works on him more than the others.

years.h: "New Slang" soundtracks a McDonald's Winter Olympics ad
years.p: James Mercer licenses New Slang to McDonald's for a 2002 Winter Olympics commercial. Indie fans and Albuquerque's alt-weekly cry foul.
years.xp: Mercer has been upfront: licensing and touring paid him more than record sales did. The money let him buy a house and move to Portland, Oregon.

years.h: Neal Langford out, Dave Hernandez in on bass
years.p: Bassist Neal Langford is gone before Chutes Too Narrow, replaced by Dave Hernandez. Jesse Sandoval told The Guardian in 2009 that Langford didn't leave, he was fired.

years.h: Burglars steal the Oh, Inverted World masters from James Mercer's house
years.p: Thieves take the HP Pavilion computer holding the mastered Oh, Inverted World files. DAT backups at the mastering house save the album, but it can never be remixed, except New Slang, which survived on a DVD.

years.h: Chutes Too Narrow, made in a Portland basement
years.p: The Shins record their second album themselves in a basement studio in Portland, cheaper than a real studio and not comfortable. It reaches No. 86 on the Billboard 200.

eras.title: Natalie Portman changes everything
eras.text: One scene in a small indie film did more for The Shins than any review. Within three years the band went from No. 86 to No. 2 on the Billboard 200, and Sub Pop had its biggest chart week ever.

years.h: Natalie Portman plays "New Slang" to Zach Braff in Garden State
years.p: In Zach Braff's Garden State, Natalie Portman's character hands him her headphones and promises New Slang will change his life. For The Shins, it does.
years.xp:
Caring Is Creepy is in the film too. Sales of both Shins albums more than doubled, colleges wanted them on campus, and Spin wrote that they became indie-rock icons almost overnight. Some early fans felt the obscurity had been part of the point.

Oh, Inverted World went on to sell 500,000 copies in the U.S.

years.h: James Mercer writes Wincing the Night Away through insomnia
years.p: Unable to sleep, James Mercer gets up in the middle of the night and works in his home studio until dawn. The album's title and its opener, Sleeping Lessons, both point at it.

years.h: Wincing the Night Away leaks three months early
years.p: A promo copy of The Shins' third album hits the internet in October, three months before release. The single Phantom Limb follows officially on November 14.

years.h: iTunes sells Wincing the Night Away two weeks early by mistake
years.p: The album is briefly, accidentally for sale on iTunes on January 9, two weeks before its street date.

years.h: The Shins play Saturday Night Live, host Jake Gyllenhaal
years.p: Ten days before Wincing the Night Away comes out, The Shins are the musical guest on Saturday Night Live.

years.h: Wincing the Night Away debuts at No. 2, Sub Pop's highest ever
years.p: Produced by James Mercer and [[Joe Chiccarelli|2a250f44-5473-4dc9-a8ba-2320fb31b2f9]], it sells more than 118,000 copies in week one. No Sub Pop record had ever charted that high on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: It was made in Mercer's basement in Oregon City and at producer [[Phil Ek|974863b2-1c82-4bb7-b23f-54ddf2713e88]]'s home in Seattle, and it topped the digital, rock, independent and Tastemakers charts the same week. Mercer has said it came out of a painful breakup and the band's sudden fame.

eras.title: James Mercer blows up the band
eras.text: After a Grammy nod, Mercer was worn out by being the center of everything. He left Sub Pop, made a record with Danger Mouse, and let go of every other Shin.

years.h: Wincing the Night Away gets a Grammy nomination
years.p: The Shins are up for Best Alternative Music Album at the Grammys. They don't win.

q: Jesse Sandoval, to the Portland Mercury
years.h: James Mercer lets go of Jesse Sandoval, Marty Crandall and Dave Hernandez
years.p: James Mercer calls parting with every other Shin an aesthetic decision. Drummer Jesse Sandoval, there from the start, tells the Portland Mercury otherwise. [[Joe Plummer|5fd1bd8e-f2b4-4f01-acc0-3423456f06ae]] of Modest Mouse takes over the drums.
years.xp:
Mercer later called it tremendously difficult. He said he'd always loved auteurs who presented themselves as bands, like Neutral Milk Hotel and Lilys, and was tired of friendships and the band's creative life revolving around him.

Mercer also moved The Shins off Sub Pop to his own label, Aural Apothecary.

years.h: James Mercer and Danger Mouse become Broken Bells
years.p: Producer Brian Burton, known as [[Danger Mouse|4b356f05-bcc2-4544-925b-fd9a1bf708be]], approaches James Mercer, and the two make music as [[Broken Bells|62d364d2-550b-420e-b918-b3bd1e4a2efc]]. Mercer likes working with new people so much he wants that feeling in The Shins too.

years.h: A new Shins: Yuuki Matthews, Jessica Dobson, Richard Swift
years.p: James Mercer rebuilds The Shins with bassist Yuuki Matthews of Crystal Skulls, guitarist [[Jessica Dobson|24d03776-9bfc-4bcf-b52f-bd316e5f9ee9]] and multi-instrumentalist [[Richard Swift|dd5f8909-245d-458b-833a-cd6b698399ce]], with Joe Plummer on drums.

eras.title: New band, same name
eras.text: The new Shins debuted at No. 3 and landed the band's biggest radio hit. Mercer then steered back toward the old sound on Heartworms, and lost a bandmate to addiction.

years.h: Port of Morrow debuts at No. 3
years.p: Produced with [[Greg Kurstin|ef2a8c11-a35a-4c61-b750-5cb29c1223f4]], who pushes James Mercer to experiment. Simple Song becomes The Shins' biggest hit, reaching the top 10 of Billboard's Alternative Songs chart.

years.h: The new Shins tape Austin City Limits
years.p: The rebuilt Shins play an episode of Austin City Limits the month Port of Morrow comes out.

years.h: Zach Braff calls again: "So Now What" for Wish I Was Here
years.p: Ten years after Garden State, The Shins record So Now What for Zach Braff's Wish I Was Here. James Mercer tells Billboard it's one of the best things he's ever done.

years.h: The Shins cover the Beatles' "The Word" for a kids' show
years.p: The Shins record The Word for Netflix's animated series Beat Bugs, built on Beatles songs.

years.h: Heartworms goes back to the old Shins palette
years.p: James Mercer says he made a deliberate effort to use the sounds he'd used historically for the band.
years.xp: In January 2018 came The Worm's Heart, a reimagined version of the whole album.

years.h: Former Shin Richard Swift dies at 41
years.p: Richard Swift dies in Tacoma, Washington. His family says the cause was complications from hepatitis plus liver and kidney distress, and that he'd struggled with alcohol addiction all his life.
years.xp: Swift played keys, bass, guitar and much more in The Shins from 2011 to 2016, toured as The Black Keys' bassist in 2014–15, and made his own records for Secretly Canadian. Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold later named him in the song Sunblind.

eras.title: Twenty-one candles for Oh, Inverted World
eras.text: The Shins spent the early 2020s going back to where it started: a remaster, a tour of the first album start to finish, a platinum plaque, and the loss of the bassist who played on it.

years.h: "The Great Divide", a new Shins single
years.p: The Shins' first new song since Heartworms.

years.h: Oh, Inverted World remastered by Bob Ludwig at 20
years.p: Sub Pop's 20th-anniversary reissue, remastered by Bob Ludwig with James Mercer assisting, in new artwork and packaging.

years.h: The Shins play Oh, Inverted World front to back on tour
years.p: Announced in May 2022, the 21st Birthday tour takes The Shins' debut, in full, across North America.

years.h: Oh, Inverted World goes platinum
years.p: The RIAA certifies The Shins' debut platinum, only the third Sub Pop album to get there.

years.h: Original Shins bassist Neal Langford dies at 50
years.p: Neal Langford, who played in Flake Music and on Oh, Inverted World, dies at 50. No cause was reported. James Mercer says Langford talked him out of his shyness and into the microphone.
years.xp: After The Shins, Langford and Marty Crandall made an EP as Sad Baby Wolf in 2013. He had been living in North Carolina with his partner.

years.h: James Mercer says a new Shins album is next
years.p: James Mercer tells Consequence his next project is a new Shins record.
